proposals.before: Yu Di, whose courtesy name was Yun'yuan, came from Henan and was descended from Shen, the Zhou Grand Preceptor enfeoffed as Duke Wen of Yan.
proposals.after: Yu Di, whose courtesy name was Yun'yuan, came from Henan and was descended from Jin, Grand Preceptor of the Northern Zhou and posthumously Duke Wen of Yan.
proposals.reason: 周 here is the Northern Zhou, not the ancient Zhou; 謹 is the given name of Grand Preceptor Yu Jin, later honored as Duke Wen of Yan.

proposals.before: Yu Di, style name Yun'yuan, was a native of Henan and a descendant of Yan Duke Wen of Zhou, the Grand Preceptor Shen.
proposals.after: Yu Di, style name Yun'yuan, was a native of Henan and a descendant of Jin, Grand Preceptor of the Northern Zhou and Duke Wen of Yan.
proposals.reason: The literal rendering makes 周 the ancient Zhou and inverts the title-name order; 燕文公謹 is Jin, Northern Zhou Grand Preceptor, Duke Wen of Yan.

proposals.before: He first entered service through hereditary privilege as a guard in the Thousand-Ox regiment, was then assigned as magistrate of Hua Yin, and was recruited as aide by the inspection commissioner Liu Wan.
proposals.after: He first entered service through hereditary privilege as a Thousand-Ox guard, was then assigned as county defender of Huayin, and was recruited as an aide by the inspection commissioner Liu Wan.
proposals.reason: 華陰尉 is a county commandant/defender (wei), not the magistrate (ling); the idiomatic 'magistrate' misstates the office.

proposals.before: When Zhenglun died, before the funeral Di surrounded his house with troops and ordered his illegitimate son to force marriage on his legitimate daughter.
proposals.after: When Zhenglun died, before the funeral Di surrounded his house with troops and ordered his illegitimate son to force a marriage on Zhenglun's legitimate daughter.
proposals.reason: 其嫡女 is Xue Zhenglun's legitimate daughter, not Yu Di's; the repeated 'his' makes the bride appear to be Di's child.

proposals.before: His second son Fang repeatedly urged his father to return to court and pay homage; he was enfeoffed as Minister of Works and Grand Councilor.
proposals.after: His second son Fang repeatedly urged his father to return to court and pay homage; Yu Di was then appointed Minister of Works and Grand Councilor.
proposals.reason: 冊拜 is an appointment, not an enfeoffment, and the silent subject of 冊拜 is Yu Di after returning, not Fang.

proposals.before: His second son Fang repeatedly urged him to return to court; Di was then appointed Minister of Works and Grand Councilor.
proposals.after: His second son Fang repeatedly urged him to return to court and pay homage; Di was then appointed Minister of Works and Grand Councilor.
proposals.reason: Chinese 歸朝入覲 includes paying court in person; the idiomatic line drops 入覲.

proposals.before: Jiyou, Vice Director of the Palace Domestic Service and Imperial Son-in-Law, had two ranks of office stripped posthumously [retroactively], and his household was ordered to reflect on their conduct.
proposals.after: Jiyou, Vice Director of the Palace Domestic Service and Imperial Son-in-Law, had two ranks of office stripped retroactively, and his household was ordered to reflect on their conduct.
proposals.reason: 追奪 means retroactive stripping of a living official's ranks, not a posthumous penalty; the gloss 'posthumously' is a mistranslation.

proposals.before: That October Di was reassigned as Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
proposals.after: In the tenth month of that year Di was reassigned as Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
proposals.reason: 十月 is a lunar month in Yuanhe 8, not the Gregorian month October.

proposals.before: He died that August and was posthumously made Grand Guardian with the posthumous name Li, "Harsh."
proposals.after: He died in the eighth month of that year and was posthumously made Grand Guardian with the posthumous name Li, "Harsh."
proposals.reason: 八月 is a lunar month in Yuanhe 13, not the Gregorian month August.

proposals.before: Yet Di, a civil official holding a post in the empire's heartland, had defied the throne and come to court only under compulsion—how can he be compared to Maozhao!
proposals.after: Yet Yu Di, a civil official holding a post in the empire's heartland, had defied the throne and come to court only under compulsion—how can he be compared to Maozhao!
proposals.reason: Chinese 於頔 is the full name; the idiomatic English drops the surname while the literal keeps Yu Di.

proposals.before: The memorials went unanswered; in the end the posthumous name Si stood.
proposals.after: The memorials went unanswered; in the end the posthumous name Si was confirmed.
proposals.reason: “Si stood” is unidiomatic for 謚為思, which means the posthumous title Si was adopted.

proposals.before: In 799 Quanliang died; the Bian troops, remembering Xuanzuo's kindness and finding Hong steady and generous, asked that he be made acting military governor; supervisor Huan memorialized the court, which approved the request out of regard for Xuanzuo.
proposals.after: In 799 Quanliang died; the Bian troops, remembering Xuanzuo's kindness and finding Hong steady and generous, asked that he be made acting military governor; they surrounded the army supervisor and asked him to memorialize the matter, and the court also granted it out of regard for Xuanzuo.
proposals.reason: 環監軍使 is the verb 環 plus 監軍使, not a person named Huan; Qu Huan 曲環 appears only in a later sentence.

proposals.before: In the fifteenth year of Zhenyuan, Quanliang died; the Bian army remembered Xuanzuo's kindness, and because Hong was also generous and steady, they jointly requested him as acting military governor; Huan, the army supervisor, requested a memorial on the matter, and the court also granted it for Xuanzuo's sake.
proposals.after: In the fifteenth year of Zhenyuan, Quanliang died; the Bian army remembered Xuanzuo's kindness, and because Hong was also generous and steady, they jointly requested him as acting military governor; they surrounded the army supervisor and asked him to memorialize the matter, and the court also granted it for Xuanzuo's sake.
proposals.reason: The literal English likewise misreads 環 as the personal name Huan.

proposals.before: He was repeatedly promoted to acting vice director and Minister of Works.
proposals.after: He was repeatedly promoted to acting Left and Right Vice Director and to Minister of Works.
proposals.reason: 左右僕射 are the Left and Right Vice Directors; the idiomatic line collapses 左右.

proposals.before: When Yan Shou was appointed campaign commander and defeated, Hong still held Bianzhou at the strategic junction of the Hebei rebels; the court feared disloyalty and wished to give him nominal command while Li Guangyan and Wu Chongyin led the actual fighting.
proposals.after: When Yan Shou was appointed campaign commander and defeated, Hong still held Bianzhou at the strategic junction of the two He rebels; the court feared disloyalty and wished to give him nominal command while Li Guangyan and Wu Chongyin led the actual fighting.
proposals.reason: 兩河 is the two He regions, not specifically Hebei.

proposals.before: Han Hong, Vice Military Governor of the Xuanwu Army with authority over military governorship affairs, Surveillance and Disposition Commissioner of Bian, Song, Bo, and Ying, Grand Master with Golden Seal and Three Excellencies, Acting Minister of Education, concurrently Palace Attendant, Commissioner with Staff for Bian Military Affairs, Prefect of Bian, Supreme Pillar of the State, Duke of Xu with a fief of three thousand households—descended spirit, outstanding talent, accumulated depth becoming vessel;
proposals.after: Han Hong, Vice Military Governor of the Xuanwu Army with authority over military governorship affairs, Surveillance and Disposition Commissioner of Bian, Song, Bo, and Ying, Grand Master Equal to the Three Excellencies, Acting Minister of Education, concurrently Palace Attendant, Commissioner with Staff for Bian Military Affairs, Prefect of Bian, Supreme Pillar of the State, Duke of Xu with a fief of three thousand households—descended spirit, outstanding talent, accumulated depth becoming vessel;
proposals.reason: 開府儀同三司 does not mention a golden seal; that wording invents 金印.

proposals.before: He died of illness that December, aged fifty-eight.
proposals.after: He died of illness in the twelfth month of that year, aged fifty-eight.
proposals.reason: 十二月 is a lunar month, not the Gregorian month December.

proposals.before: Gongwu, from Xuanwu Cavalry and Infantry Director, led troops to execute Cai; when the rebels were pacified, he was made Acting Right Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, Prefect of Fu, and Military Governor of Fu and Fang.
proposals.after: Gongwu, from Xuanwu Cavalry and Infantry Director, led troops to punish Cai; when the rebels were pacified, he was made Acting Right Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, Prefect of Fu, and Military Governor of Fu and Fang.
proposals.reason: 誅蔡 means a punitive campaign against the Cai rebels, not execution of the place Cai.

proposals.before: His father Jin served as grand guardian of the heir apparent.
proposals.after: His father Jin served as Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent.
proposals.reason: 太子詹事 is the household supervisor of the heir apparent, not 太子太保 (grand guardian).

proposals.before: His father Jin was Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
proposals.after: His father Jin was Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent.
proposals.reason: 太子詹事 is misrendered as Grand Guardian; that office is 太子太保.

proposals.before: With the Chenxu army he routed the rebels at Jinxiang, took Yutai, and killed or captured tens of thousands; for this he was promoted to censor-in-chief.
proposals.after: With the Chenxu army he routed the rebels at Jinxiang, took Yutai, and killed or captured tens of thousands; for this he was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief.
proposals.reason: 御史中丞 is the vice censor-in-chief; 御史大夫 is censor-in-chief.

proposals.before: With the Chen and Xu armies he greatly defeated the rebels at Jinxiang, captured Yutai, and captives and slain numbered in the tens of thousands; for merit he was transferred to Censor-in-Chief.
proposals.after: With the Chen and Xu armies he greatly defeated the rebels at Jinxiang, captured Yutai, and captives and slain numbered in the tens of thousands; for merit he was transferred to Vice Censor-in-Chief.
proposals.reason: 御史中丞 is not Censor-in-Chief.

proposals.before: During the Yuanhe reign, after imperial forces killed Wu Yuanji, Li Shidao joined the Cai rebels in harassing the court's armies and repeatedly raided Xu; Military Governor Li Yuan put all his infantry and cavalry under Zhixing to repel them.
proposals.after: During the Yuanhe reign, while imperial forces campaigned to destroy Wu Yuanji, Li Shidao joined the Cai rebels in harassing the court's armies and repeatedly raided Xu; Military Governor Li Yuan put all his infantry and cavalry under Zhixing to repel them.
proposals.reason: 誅吳元濟 here marks the campaign concurrent with Li Shidao's raids, not a completed execution after which the raids began.

proposals.before: In the thirteenth year (818), after imperial forces killed Li Shidao, Zhixing led eight thousand Xu troops to join the allied armies in the advance.
proposals.after: In the thirteenth year (818), as the imperial army moved to destroy Li Shidao, Zhixing led eight thousand Xu troops to join the allied armies in the advance.
proposals.reason: The following capture of Yutai shows Zhixing's advance as part of destroying Li Shidao, not an action after the killing was already finished.

proposals.before: Chi developed a carbuncle on his head and entrusted the troops to his senior staff officer Li Zhi.
proposals.after: Chi developed a carbuncle on his head and entrusted the troops to his steward Li Zhi.
proposals.reason: 紀綱 here is a household steward or confidential aide, not specifically a senior staff officer.

proposals.before: Zhixing had already taken the lead. When his officers heard Qun's instructions, they were incensed; they led the returning troops, forced the gates, and killed more than ten officers who opposed them.
proposals.after: Zhixing had already taken the foremost position. When the staff heard this their resolve was stirred; they led the returning troops, forced the gates, and killed more than ten men in the army who were not of their faction.
proposals.reason: 心動 is stirred or shaken resolve, not 'incensed'; 異己者 are factional opponents in the army, and 首處 matches being already in place rather than merely taking the lead.

proposals.before: At first Tongjie's defiance was sustained by aid from Ji and Wang Tingcou, and imperial campaigns had failed for years.
proposals.after: At first Tongjie's wild defiance of orders was sustained by aid from Wang Tingcou, and the imperial armies had failed for years.
proposals.reason: 濟之以王廷湊 means Tongjie was aided by Wang Tingcou; 濟 is the verb 'to succor', not Ji Prefecture.

proposals.before: At first Tongjie was wild and defiant in offending orders; Ji Prefecture aided him together with Wang Tingcou; the imperial army for years had no success.
proposals.after: At first Tongjie was wild and defiant in offending orders; he was aided by Wang Tingcou; the imperial army for years had no success.
proposals.reason: The literal rendering invents Ji Prefecture from the verb 濟; the only named aider is Wang Tingcou.

proposals.before: The encomium says: Yu's son was pure and wild, lightly violating constant law.
proposals.after: The encomium says: Yu was unrestrained and reckless, lightly violating the constant laws.
proposals.reason: 於子 addresses Yu himself, not 'Yu's son'; 清狂 is unrestrained recklessness, not 'pure and wild'.

decisions.reason: 周太師燕文公謹 is Yu Jin of the Northern Zhou, Grand Preceptor and posthumously Duke Wen of Yan; 謹 is Jin, not Shen, and 文公 is a posthumous ducal title rather than a living enfeoffment as Duke Wen.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 周太師燕文公謹之後也

decisions.reason: The literal line treats 周 as the ancient Zhou, inverts 燕文公謹, and misreads 謹 as Shen; Jin, Northern Zhou Grand Preceptor and Duke Wen of Yan, matches the Chinese order.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 周太師燕文公謹之後也

decisions.reason: 華陰尉 is the county defender (尉), not the magistrate (令); county defender of Huayin restores the office named after 調授.
After 正倫卒 and 圍其宅, 其嫡女 is Zhenglun's legitimate daughter; the repeated his makes the bride appear to be Di's child.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 頔以兵圍其宅，令孽男逼娶其嫡女

decisions.reason: 冊拜司空、平章事 follows 歸朝入覲 and appoints Yu Di, not Fang; 冊拜 is an appointment by diploma, not an enfeoffment.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 屢諷其父歸朝入覲，冊拜司空、平章事

decisions.reason: 歸朝入覲 names return to court and a personal audience; the idiomatic line drops 入覲.
追奪兩任官階 strips a living official's ranks retroactively; the following household 循省 and the brothers' suspension show Jiyou is alive, so posthumously is wrong.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 追奪兩任官階，令其家循省

decisions.reason: 其年十月 is the tenth lunar month of that year (Yuanhe 8), not the Gregorian month October.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 頔其年十月，改授太子賓客

decisions.reason: 其年八月 is the eighth lunar month of Yuanhe 13, not the Gregorian month August.
於頔 is Yu Di, already named in the chapter; using Di after that identification is accurate English and does not change the person, office, or comparison with Maozhao.
疏奏不報，竟謚為思 means the unanswered memorials left the posthumous name Si in force; Si stood is accurate, and was confirmed is only a stylistic swap.
環監軍使請表其事 is the verb 環 plus the army supervisor, not a man named Huan; 曲環 is a different person only in the next sentence.
The literal field likewise turns 環 into the personal name Huan; the Bian troops surrounded the army supervisor and asked him to memorialize.
檢校左右僕射 names both Left and Right Vice Director; collapsing 左右 to a single vice director omits the paired offices.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 累授檢校左右僕射、司空

decisions.reason: 當兩河賊之沖要 is the two He regions, not Hebei alone.
開府儀同三司 is Grand Master Equal to the Three Excellencies; Golden Seal invents 金印, which is not in the edict.
其年十二月 is the twelfth lunar month of that year, not the Gregorian month December.
將兵誅蔡 is a punitive campaign against the Cai rebels, not execution of the place Cai; 賊平 then marks the rebels' pacification.
太子詹事 is Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent, not Grand Guardian (太子太保).
The literal line repeats the same office error; 太子詹事 is not Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
以功遷御史中丞 is promotion to Vice Censor-in-Chief; 御史大夫 would be Censor-in-Chief.
The literal field likewise renders 御史中丞 as Censor-in-Chief; Vice Censor-in-Chief is the office named.
王師誅吳元濟 frames the Yuanhe campaign; 李師道與蔡賊謀撓沮王師 is concurrent harassment, so after imperial forces killed wrongly completes Wu Yuanji's death before the raids.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 王師誅吳元濟，李師道與蔡賊謀撓沮王師

decisions.reason: 十三年，王師誅李師道 is followed by 進擊 and the Jinxiang–Yutai fighting, then 賊平; Zhixing's advance belongs to the campaign, not a sequel after Li Shidao had already been killed.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 十三年，王師誅李師道，智興率徐軍八千會諸道之師進擊

decisions.reason: 紀綱李質 is a steward or confidential household officer, not a senior staff officer such as a 司馬 or 都押衙.

decisions.after: Zhixing had already taken the lead. When his staff heard Qun's instructions, they were stirred; they led the returning troops, forced the gates, and killed more than ten men in the army who were not of their faction.
decisions.reason: 心動 is stirred or shaken, not incensed, and 軍中異己者 are factional opponents in the army rather than officers only. The proposed foremost position and the staff heard this are vaguer than 聞之 pointing back to Qun's orders; keep taken the lead and name those instructions.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 智興既首處，賓僚聞之心動，率歸師斬關而入，殺軍中異己者十余人

decisions.reason: 濟之以王廷湊 uses 濟 as the verb to succor, with Wang Tingcou as the only named aider; Ji Prefecture is invented from that verb.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 同捷狂桀犯命，濟之以王廷湊

decisions.reason: The literal line likewise turns 濟之 into Ji Prefecture aiding Tongjie together with Wang Tingcou; only Wang Tingcou is named.
於子 is an address to Yu himself, not Yu's son, and 清狂 is unrestrained recklessness rather than pure and wild.

claimRetractions.reason: Accepted r0023 shows 王師誅吳元濟 dates the campaign during which Li Shidao still plotted with the Cai rebels; this unit does not report Wu Yuanji as already executed.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 王師誅吳元濟，李師道與蔡賊謀撓沮王師

claimRetractions.reason: Accepted r0024 shows 王師誅李師道 in year 13 launches the allied advance; 賊平 comes only after Jinxiang and Yutai, so this unit does not report Li Shidao as already executed.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 十三年，王師誅李師道，智興率徐軍八千會諸道之師進擊

claimRevisions.reason: Accepted r0001 restores 謹 as Jin; the extracted English given name Shen was created by the mistranslation.

value.statement: descended from Grand Preceptor Shen, Duke Wen of Yan
descended from Grand Preceptor Jin, Duke Wen of Yan

claimRevisions.reason: The lineage statement repeated Grand Preceptor Shen from the bad English; the ancestor named in 燕文公謹 is Jin.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 周太師燕文公謹之後也

claimRevisions.reason: With 誅 read as the concurrent campaign, this unit supports Wu Yuanji as the target of an imperial punitive campaign, not a completed destruction before the Xu raids.
Year-13 誅李師道 is the campaign Zhixing joined; the unit does not yet record Li Shidao as destroyed.
